😊 I'm glad to hear that you are interested in **Spring Boot**! It is a powerful framework for developing web applications using the Java programming language, and it comes packed with lots of functionality out-of-the-box thanks to its extensive ecosystem. Here’s how we can approach your learning journey:

1. Understand Basic Concepts in Spring Framework (Referencing "Spring Fundamentals for Beginners" online course) – This will provide a solid foundation of understanding the core concepts, such as dependency injection and aspect-oriented programming which are essential when working with **Spring Boot**.

2. Introduction to Java: Set up your development environment - Installing an IDE like IntelliJ IDEA or Eclipse is recommended for better experience (You can find setup guides on the official Spring website). Familiarize yourself with basic syntax and project structure before diving into Spring-specific concepts.

3. Learn Maven Project Structure – Read up on "Getting Started with a Simple Java Application" to understand how your projects are structured using Maven (a build automation tool) which is the standard for **Spring Boot** applications. You can practice setting up new projects and experimenting with dependencies, plugins, etc.

4. Explore Spring MVC – The official "Learning Spring Framework" documentation has a detailed section on creating web applications using Spring's Model-View-Controller (MVC) framework which will be crucial for your internship project portfolio piece involving **Spring Boot** backend development: [https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/reference/html/web.html](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/reference/html/web.html)

5. Create a Basic Spring Boot Application – Follow the "Spring Boot in Action" book for step by step instructions on setting up your first **Spring Boot** application and understanding how to run it locally as well as deploying it onto servers like Tomcat or Jetty (You can find this guide at [https://www.springgarden.com/guides/getting_started](https://www.springgarden.com/guides/getting_started)).

6. Start a Portfolio Project – Begin with "Hello, World!" examples and gradually expand your project to include RESTful services using Spring's `@RestController` annotations (You can find sample projects in the **Spring Boot Actuator** guide: [https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/current/reference/htmlsingle/#howto-create-a-simple-web-application](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/current/reference/htmlsingle/#howto-create-a-simple-web-application)).

7. Implement CRUD Operations – Look into the "Building Web Applications with Spring" guide for creating full stack applications, including a frontend that communicates with your **Spring Boot** backend to handle Create, Read, Update and Delete operations (You can find this information in [https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/reference/htmlsingle/#mvc](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/reference/htmlsingle/#mvc)).

8. Review Best Practices – Read about maintainability and security best practices in the "Spring Security for Beginners" guide (Link: [https://www.baeldung.com/spring-security](https://www01_29673541x,yahoo image viewer)

I hope this roadmap will not only prepare you to learn **Spring Boot** effectively but also impress potential internship supervisors with your hands-on experience and understanding of the framework. Remember that practice is key! Good luck on embarking upon this exciting learning journey, and feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need further guidance along the way. 😊 Take your time.
